title: IDSA Uncomplicated Cystitis — First-line agents
text: For acute uncomplicated cystitis in women, first-line agents are nitrofurantoin monohydrate/macrocrystals 100 mg orally twice daily for 5 days, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole one double-strength tablet twice daily for 3 days if local resistance rates do not exceed 20%, or fosfomycin tromethamine 3 g orally in a single dose. Fluoroquinolones are not recommended as first-line empiric therapy when alternatives exist due to resistance and adverse effects. Adjust for renal function; avoid nitrofurantoin if CrCl below 30 mL/min.

title: IDSA/ATS Community-Acquired Pneumonia — Outpatient
text: Previously healthy outpatient without comorbidities: amoxicillin 1 g three times daily, doxycycline 100 mg twice daily, or a macrolide only in areas with pneumococcal macrolide resistance below 25%. With comorbidities or risk factors: amoxicillin-clavulanate plus macrolide, or respiratory fluoroquinolone. Duration typically 5 days if clinically improving. Reserve broad-spectrum and anti-pseudomonal agents for inpatient or risk factors.

title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign — Empiric antibiotics
text: Administer empiric broad-spectrum antimicrobials within 1 hour of recognition for sepsis or septic shock. Use local antibiogram and epidemiology to select agents. Reassess at 48–72 hours for de-escalation based on cultures, clinical improvement, and infection source control. Shortest effective duration reduces AMR selection pressure.

title: WHO AWaRe — Stewardship principle
text: WHO AWaRe categorizes antibiotics into Access (first- and second-choice for common infections), Watch (higher resistance potential — prioritize stewardship), and Reserve (last-resort — restrict to confirmed susceptible organisms). Hospital AMS programs should target ≥60% Access agent use where clinically appropriate and require justification for Reserve agents.

title: India empirical UTI — fluoroquinolone resistance context
text: ICMR AMRSN and WHO GLASS data from Indian laboratories report high non-susceptibility of E. coli to fluoroquinolones in urinary isolates, often exceeding 65–75% in aggregate tertiary-care surveillance. Empiric ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin for UTI should not be default without local susceptibility data supporting use. Prefer nitrofurantoin, fosfomycin, or TMP-SMX when local antibiogram susceptibility exceeds 80%.

title: MRSA bloodstream infection — treatment
text: For MRSA bacteremia or severe infection: vancomycin or daptomycin IV; linezolid for pneumonia when alternatives limited. Outpatient purulent SSTI with MRSA: TMP-SMX, clindamycin, or doxycycline per local susceptibility. Obtain blood cultures before antibiotics when feasible. ID consultation recommended for persistent bacteremia, endocarditis, or prosthetic device infection.

title: ESBL-producing Enterobacterales
text: ESBL-producing Enterobacterales: carbapenems (meropenem, ertapenem) are preferred for serious infections when beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitor activity is unreliable. Piperacillin-tazobactam may be inadequate for high-inoculum ESBL bacteremia. For uncomplicated ESBL UTI, oral fosfomycin or nitrofurantoin may be options if susceptible. De-escalate per culture and MIC when safe.

title: Clinical data minimization for AI CDS (India DPDP aligned)
text: Clinical decision support for antibiotic stewardship should use minimum necessary data: age, sex, weight, creatinine, diagnosis, allergies, medications, culture results, and pseudonymous identifier. Direct identifiers (name, Aadhaar, phone, address) must not be transmitted to cloud AI processors. Physician attestation and audit logs support accountability under hospital ethics review.
